title: Defect Cavity Microresonator for Narrowband 8-13 μm Peak
scientific_hypothesis: A Fabry-Perot microcavity formed by HfO2/SiO2 Bragg mirrors with a central defect layer will produce a sharp high-emissivity resonance within the 8-13 μm atmospheric window while maintaining very low emissivity outside the resonance, including the 3-5 μm band.
design_principle: Two Bragg mirror stacks sandwich a cavity layer whose optical thickness creates a resonant mode within the mirror bandgap. This produces a narrow transmission (high emissivity) peak at the cavity resonance wavelength while the mirrors suppress emission elsewhere.
proposed_topology: air | (hfo2 | sio2)_4 | hfo2 (cavity) | (sio2 | hfo2)_4 | si substrate, exactly 17 layers total (8 mirror layers + 1 cavity + 8 mirror layers)
design_variables: mirror layer thicknesses (8 pairs, 16 layers) at quarter-wave for 10500 nm, cavity layer thickness (1 layer) tuned for resonance position within 8000-13000 nm
soft_objectives: maximize peak emissivity at cavity resonance within 8000-13000 nm
position resonance near 10500 nm center of atmospheric window
manufacturing_considerations: cavity thickness precision critical for resonance positioning
Bragg mirrors require consistent layer thickness control
theory_basis: Defect mode in photonic bandgap structures
Literature L08 on quasi-optical microcavity, L19 on resonator structures for emissivity tuning
expected_advantages: Very high peak emissivity achievable at resonance
Literature L08 and L19 support microcavity approach for spectral control
known_risks: Narrow resonance may not cover full 8-13 μm window, reducing integrated emissivity
Resonance position sensitive to thickness errors
L19 notes phase-change materials not used here, limiting tunability
execution_request_english: Design a defect-cavity multilayer dielectric stack on silicon substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat))_4 | hfo2_cavity | (SiO2 (Kischkat) | hfo2)_4 | si, exactly 17 layers total. Optimize mirror layer thicknesses (16 layers) at quarter-wave for 10500 nm, and cavity layer thickness (1 layer) to position resonance within 8000-13000 nm band. Target: maximize peak emissivity at resonance, minimize emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band. Wavelength range for evaluation: 3000-13000 nm. Polarization: unpolarized (average TE and TM). Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal). Material refractive indices from catalog datasets for hfo2, SiO2 (Kischkat), and si. Total layer count fixed at 17.
